{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 supports comparisons of performance on unfamiliar grid problems when exposure, evaluation version, settings and spending conditions are comparable. Worked examples and exact output requirements give the task a clear operational definition, while developer review and human testing informed puzzle selection. Human difficulty matching does not establish equal difficulty for AI systems. Scoring is explicit: each input receives credit for an exact match within two attempts, and input success fractions are averaged within problems before averaging across problems. Consequently, the reported score is not simply the percentage of problems fully solved. Verified evaluations document conditions, but a single run and missing repeatability estimates limit interpretation of small differences. Public materials and revision records support inspection, although complete marking validation and retrospective score updates are absent. The supplied evidence supports conclusions about grid-task performance; broader reasoning and intelligence claims remain unresolved.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The tasks require inferring grid transformations from examples and producing exact outputs, directly supporting evaluation of performance on this task format.",
        "Puzzle selection included human solving data and checks for repeated solution rules, providing evidence of deliberate construction.",
        "The three evaluation sets were selected for similar human difficulty using the human study; this supports that specific matching claim.",
        "The inspected software gives partial problem credit when only some new inputs are solved, while requiring exact matches for each credited input.",
        "Verified evaluations specify settings and spending limits, supporting comparisons within documented conditions.",
        "Public problems, software, marking tests and dated revisions permit inspection of substantial parts of the benchmark."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Corrections to coloured squares and unclear examples show that released materials required repairs.",
        "Software scores and the dataset's definition of a fully solved problem differ, creating a reporting ambiguity if both are described as problem-solving rates.",
        "Verified evaluations use one run, leaving individual reported results vulnerable to unquantified run variation.",
        "Public evaluation problems are accessible, and the policy acknowledges possible leakage of hidden problems.",
        "Revision records do not recalculate every affected AI score, complicating comparisons across material versions."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Repeated identical evaluations and uncertainty estimates are needed to judge score stability and small differences.",
        "Systematic studies of instructions, grid presentation and software changes are needed to establish robustness.",
        "AI-specific evidence is needed to determine whether the human-matched test sets are comparable for AI systems.",
        "A complete independent marking-system evaluation is absent; the preparer inspected selected public tests.",
        "Stronger exposure checks and tests of unintended solution routes are needed to establish that scores reflect unfamiliar problem solving.",
        "Evidence connecting scores to language, social interaction or real-world work is absent.",
        "The complete reporting archive was not checked, so the availability and completeness of all claimed outputs remain unverified."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "AI success means producing correct grid outputs under specified attempt and resource conditions; interpreting it as general or human-like intelligence expands beyond the supplied evidence.",
        "Calling an evaluation problem unfamiliar assumes the AI has not encountered it; public availability and possible leakage make unfamiliarity conditional.",
        "A score described as problems solved must be understood as the average of within-problem input success fractions, unless full-problem completion is separately reported.",
        "Similar difficulty for people cannot be reinterpreted as similar difficulty or score stability for AI systems."
      ],
      "closing_note": "No puzzle solving is required. Reports should clarify whether 'solved' refers to individual inputs, fractional problem scores or fully completed problems, and identify the evaluation version and conditions."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA supports examining how AI systems answer selected Formula SAE rule and vehicle-document questions under specified information conditions. Real engineering materials and practitioner contributions give the tasks practical relevance, but one rulebook and six unevenly represented groups provide limited coverage of engineering work. Review procedures offer some quality control without establishing remaining error rates. Scoring combines different methods, including text similarity that can penalize formatting or valid answers omitted from references. Equal weighting of groups makes the overall result depend strongly on small groups despite their limited evidence. Comparisons also involve differences in information supply, so they assess AI systems together with retrieval and context provision. Missing repeatability estimates, incomplete historical records and exposure controls constrain fine rankings and reproduction. Results do not establish general engineering competence or performance on other documents.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "The six groups cover rule finding, terminology, component identification, dimensions and performance checks, supporting analysis of these specified activities.",
        "Real competition rules, designs and test data connect the questions to practical engineering materials.",
        "Additional reviewers checked manually written questions with stated exceptions, providing partial evidence of content checking.",
        "The software equally weights six groups, so the overall score summarizes that weighting choice.",
        "Experiments changing passages and visual information provide evidence about sensitivity to those particular changes.",
        "Public questions, instructions, scoring code and some responses allow partial inspection of the evaluation."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "Coverage is narrow and uneven: individual-rule retrieval has 1,192 questions, while performance checking has only 16.",
        "Question review had exceptions, and some explanations received only a check that they supported the yes/no decision.",
        "Formatting and reference-answer omissions affect credit, including missing commas and valid related rules absent from supplied answers.",
        "Systems receive different information, including whole rulebooks or retrieved passages, complicating attribution of differences to the AI alone.",
        "All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes response to earn decision credit on that portion; no AI is shown to have used this strategy.",
        "One released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding paper question count.",
        "Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every result, limiting exact reproduction."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "Reviewer disagreement rates and remaining answer-error estimates are needed to assess reference quality.",
        "Comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency evidence is absent, as is evidence that group or overall scores measure distinct underlying skills.",
        "Identical repeated runs and uncertainty estimates are needed to assess close rankings; changing passage sets does not isolate repeat-run variation.",
        "A human-engineer baseline was not reported.",
        "A protected test set, systematic training-overlap checks and clear training and repeat-submission rules were not established.",
        "A clear record of revision effects on scores, a licence file and complete reuse rules were not found in the inspected materials.",
        "Evidence of performance transfer to other technical documents and real engineering projects is absent."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "AI performance in the comparisons means performance of the model together with its supplied context or retrieval process; interpreting differences as model ability alone changes the evaluated object.",
        "Text-similarity credit measures agreement with reference wording as well as answer content; it cannot automatically be read as engineering correctness.",
        "An equally weighted overall score summarizes six differently scored groups; interpreting it as one established engineering-understanding ability requires additional evidence.",
        "Success on these Formula SAE tasks cannot be expanded into demonstrated competence across engineering documents or projects.",
        "Correct yes/no answers on the compliant scale-bar subset do not by themselves demonstrate that the AI measured dimensions or applied the rule."
      ],
      "closing_note": "No engineering problem solving is required. Reports should specify supplied information, scoring methods and software version. Missing licence or reuse documentation in the inspected sources does not establish that reuse is prohibited."
    }
  ]
}
